citation.title: Topology Optimization via Frequency Tuning of Neural Design Representations
citation.authors: Nikan Doosti, Julian Panetta, Vahid Babaei

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The Fourier-feature neural design representation produces structures with stiffness comparable to or better than standard finite-element density-based optimization, while requiring more optimization iterations.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No speed-up is claimed; Section 5.4 says the neural method takes longer than the voxel baseline.
claim.alternatives: Section 5.4 and Figure 6 compare compliance with voxel-based OC and a CNN method; Section 5.6 reports per-iteration solver times, not a method-level speed-up.

baseline.classical_method: voxel-density SIMP with optimality criteria and filtering (Section 5.4)
baseline.implementation: traditional voxel-based method based on Andreassen et al. 2011; both methods evaluated using the paper's FEM solver (Sections 3.1, 5.4)
baseline.solver: sparse Cholesky for 2D; multigrid-preconditioned conjugate gradient for 3D (Sections 3.1, 5.6)
baseline.hardware_classical: AMD Ryzen 5950X CPU for benchmarks; exact baseline allocation not separately stated (Section 5.6)
baseline.hardware_ml: AMD Ryzen 5950X CPU and Nvidia Quadro RTX 8000 GPU; network operations may run on CPU for large 3D cases (Section 5.6)
baseline.problem_size: 300 x 100 and 250 x 125 2D examples; 320 x 160 x 80 and 256 x 128 x 128 3D examples (Sections 5.4-5.6)
baseline.classical_iterations: voxel-based method converges around 300 iterations in Figure 6 examples (Section 5.4)
baseline.classical_time: not stated as total method time; Section 5.6 gives neural-method FE solver times of 0.161 s and 0.164 s per 2D iteration
baseline.ml_time: not stated as total method time; up to 5000 optimization iterations and 0.161/0.164 s average 2D FE solve per iteration (Sections 5.4-5.6)
baseline.training_time: not applicable: per-problem neural optimization has no offline training (Sections 4, 6)
baseline.quality_metric: FE-computed compliance/stiffness and volume budget (Sections 3.1, 5.4, Figure 6)
baseline.quality_gap: Figure 6: reported compliances are near or below voxel baseline; a single aggregate numeric gap is not stated in text

R1.evidence: Conclusion and Section 5.4: primary comparison concerns stiffness, with longer neural computation acknowledged.

R2.evidence: Section 5.4: no neural speed advantage is asserted in the primary outcome.

R3.evidence: Sections 4 and 6: network parameters are optimized for each design, without offline dataset training.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.1 and 5.4: returned designs are evaluated with an FE compliance solver and constrained by a volume penalty; infeasible-design or failed-run frequency is not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Figure 6 compares two 2D load cases; Figures 7-9 show 3D examples; no aggregate case count stated

notes: Publisher PDF returned HTTP 403; author-hosted full text was read at https://julianpanetta.com/pdf/toftndr.pdf. Author's public code is at https://github.com/Nikronic/ndr; no license was visible, so runnable licensed retest status was not established.
